item.title: Permit sought for P.F. Chang’s as Santa Rosa mall revives drive-lane project
item.description: A Santa Rosa planning panel is set to hold a hearing Feb. 12 on a proposed drive lane in front of the downtown mall. Meanwhile, a construction permit for the popular Asian American fusion restaurant at Santa Rosa Plaza is under review.

item.title: Seahawks get their turn at Super Bowl Opening Night
item.description: Super Bowl Opening Night is over, with Drake Maye, Sam Darnold and other Super Bowl participants meeting with thousands of reporters from across the globe in a zany spectacle that kicks off the week’s festivities on Monday night.

item.title: Patriots and Seahawks kick off Super Bowl festivities with a quieter, calmer, tamer Opening Night
item.description: Maybe the game itself will live up to the hype, because Super Bowl Opening Night was calmer than usual.

item.title: Seahawks’ Super Bowl 60 opening night: Darnold compliments 49ers, Seattle at home in Bay
item.description: Receiver Mack Hollins gives his take on theory about electrical substation near Levi's Stadium. Plus, offensive lineman Gray Zabel discusses his unusual childhood chores at Super Bowl media night.

item.title: Seahawks’ Klint Kubiak focused on Super Bowl, not Raiders job
item.description: Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak said his entire focus this week is on beating the New England Patriots in the Super Bowl and not on a future that is expected to see him land a job as head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders.

item.title: Ryan Donato scores twice as the Blackhawks beat the Sharks 6-3
item.description: Ryan Donato had two goals and two assists, and the Chicago Blackhawks beat the San Jose Sharks 6-3 on Monday night.

item.title: Mariners acquire All-Star Brendan Donovan from Cardinals in three-team trade with Rays
item.description: The Seattle Mariners acquired All-Star infielder/outfielder Brendan Donovan from the St. Louis Cardinals on Monday night in a three-team trade with the Tampa Bay Rays.

item.title: Major League Baseball salary increase slowed to 1.4% in 2025 while setting record at $4.7 million
item.description: The rate of increase for Major League Baseball’s average salary slowed to 1.4% last year while setting a record average at $4,721,393, according to final figures from the players’ association.
